questions.question: The successive discounts of 10%, 30% and 25% is equivalent to a single discount of _______ (correct to a nearest whole number).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Successive discounts: 10%, 30%, 25%

**Concept Used:**

Successive discounts can be calculated by

Final discount = 1 - (1 - D₁)(1 - D₂)(1 - D₃)

**Solution:**

Final discount = 1 - (1 - 0.10)(1 - 0.30)(1 - 0.25)

⇒ Final discount = 1 - (0.9)(0.7)(0.75)

⇒ Final discount = 1 - 0.4725

⇒ Final discount = 0.5275

⇒ Final discount = 52.75% ≈ 53%

**∴ The successive discounts of 10%, 30%, and 25% are equivalent to a single discount of 53%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Successive discount can be calculated by

Equivalent Discount = D1 + D2 - (D₁times D₂)/(100)

**Calculation:**

Successive discounts of 10% and 30%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 10 + 30 - (10times 30)/(100) = 37%

Successive discounts of 37% and 25%

⇒ Final Discount = 37 + 25 - (37×25)/(100)

⇒ Final Discount = 62 - 9.25 = 52.75 ≈ 53%

∴ The successive discounts of 10%, 30%, and 25% are equivalent to a single discount of 53%.

questions.question: The difference in selling price of an article when it is sold at 20% profit and 18% loss is Rs 570. If it is sold at 12% loss, then what will be the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
**Short Trick:**

(20 + 18)% of CP = 570

CP = 1500

Required SP = 1500 × (100 - 12)/100 = Rs. 1320

**Detailed Solution:**

Let the cost price be 100x.

⇒ Selling price when sold at 12% profit = 100x × 120% = 120x

⇒ Selling price when sold at 18% loss = 100x × 82% = 82x

⇒ The difference in selling price when sold at 20% Profit and when sold at 18% Loss = 570

⇒ (120x - 82x) = 570

⇒ 38x = 570

⇒ 100x = 1500

⇒ Selling price when sold at 12% loss = cost price × (100 - 12)%

⇒ Selling price when sold at 12% loss = 1500 88% = Rs. 1320

∴ Selling price at 12% loss will be Rs. 1320.

questions.question: By selling 50 items, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 10 items. What is his gain percent?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When Profit = SP of x items, then CP (in terms of units) = Total items − x.

Profit = 10 units; Total items = 50 units.

⇒ CP = 50 − 10 = 40 units.

⇒ Gain % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (10 ÷ 40) × 100.

⇒ Gain % = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of items sold = 50

Gain = Selling Price of 10 items

**Formula Used:**

Gain = Total Selling Price (SP) − Total Cost Price (CP)

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 CP (40 units)
 Profit (10)
 

 Total SP (50 units)
 Profit % = (10 / 40) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 item be ₹1.

⇒ SP of 50 items = ₹50.

⇒ Gain = SP of 10 items = ₹10.

⇒ We know, CP = SP − Gain.

⇒ CP of 50 items = 50 − 10 = ₹40.

⇒ Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100.

⇒ Gain % = (10 ÷ 40) × 100.

⇒ Gain % = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Gain/Loss on Selling Price

If a shopkeeper loses the SP of x items by selling n items, then Loss % = [x ÷ (n + x)] × 100.

Gain/Loss on Cost Price

If a shopkeeper gains the CP of x items by selling n items, then Gain % = (x ÷ n) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100.

⇒ Cost price for Soni = Cost price for Raju/(1 + Profit% of Soni) = ₹5,500/(1 + 10/100) = ₹5,000

**Hence, the cost price of the mobile for Soni is ₹5,000.**

questions.question: Manoj buys 15 pencils for Rs. 12 and sells them at the rate of Rs. 1.50/pencil. What is his profit percentage?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SP of 1 pencil = ₹1.50

Profit ratio = 15 − 8 = 7

Profit % = (7 ÷ 8) × 100 = 87.50%

Total CP of 15 pencils = ₹12

SP of 1 pencil = ₹1.50

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Total SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total SP for 15 pencils = 15 × 1.50 = ₹22.50

⇒ Profit = 22.50 − 12 = ₹10.50

⇒ Profit % = (10.50 ÷ 12) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1050 ÷ 12) = 87.50%

**∴ The correct answer is 87.50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, equivalent discount = (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

questions.question: By selling a plot of land for ₹5,45,000 a person loses 8%. At what price should he sell it to gain 12%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of a plot = ₹5,45,000

Loss = 8%

Expected gain = 12%

**Concept:**

The cost price is calculated by (Selling Price / (1 - Loss%)). The new selling price for the desired gain is (Cost Price × (1 + Gain%)).

**Solution:**

⇒ Cost price = ₹5,45,000 / (1 - 0.08) = ₹5,92,391.30

⇒ New selling price = ₹5,92,391.30 × (1 + 0.12) = ₹6,63,478.25

**Hence, to gain 12%, he should sell it for ₹6,63,478.25.**
